A Book By Its Cover (1968 film about leather bookbinding)

Description of this video:

Leather binding and the embellishment of books was once a dying skill, but recently has enjoyed a renewed popularity. People today decorate books they treasure; also custom leather bookbinding can be a lucrative hobby. The resulting works of art display the jewel-like precision of the tooling and gold leafing that is found on few books today. This classic documentary introduces viewers to two master craftsmen, L.E. Hertzberg, President of Hertzberg New Method, Inc., and Fred James, Secretary and Treasurer of Hertzberg Craftsmen, who illustrate the painstaking process involved. First, Mr. James guides viewers step-by-step through the process of binding a book in leather; then Mr. Hertzberg continues the tooling process using hand-made tools that have been passed down through his family for over 100 years. The end result is a beautiful leather-bound book with gold tooling of the hinge and spine that will give a book permanence and beauty. Produced by Iowa State University.

I'm an atheist because I don't need someone else's superstitions. I have my own.

I'm not going to try to convert you I just want to weigh in my opinion. The most widely agreed definition to god would be the creator of the universe. Being that science has recently shown the universe had a beginning that means it would have required a cause external to itself, which whatever that may be would be god to me. I'm not religious or anything but I do believe in an intelligent creator

Science hasn't shown the universe was created from the big bang, I think I'm safe in saying it's the most accepted model we have of the universe being here. However, the fact the universe is here and inflated to its present form doesn't necessitate a creator. Furthermore, one of the interesting models that has been proposed, and I think fits with the 126Gev value given to the higgs Boson is the cyclical universe. The idea that there are continual big bangs. Which for me seems to be a much more elegant explanation of the universe than a magical creator.

The entire theory of the big bang is that space, time and matter was created from the big bang. Now how would the singularity which would have existed outside of time have caused itself when time is a necessity for cause and effect? The singularity logically requires a cause that was external to itself meaning there is something else outside our physical universe.
The idea that some entity just came to exist and happened to have the power to create something so vast that we can't even begin to comprehend it, just sounds stupid.
That's the thing about an eternal god though, it never came into existence because it had always existed. It would be eternal meaning having no beginning or end.

I used to be a Christian, but then I ended up boots on ground in Iraq as a medic when I was 18. No prayers were answered. No good things happened at all, only death and evil. I saw the worst living conditions I've ever seen and the most stuck up and self centered human beings I've ever met. It caused some interesting changes in my thought process as well as that initial little bit of doubt about that loving being up on a cloud. I cam home after a year of putting pieces of my family in bags and sending them home, of watching children get used to transport HME in bicycles, a phone stuck in their backpack they didn't know about to blow them up if the Americans got wise about it, watching people pull copper pipes out of a hospital we built them to make EFPs to try to kill us with. And those people were just as religious as people back in the states I grew up around. So I examined myself and my doubts and looked into religions from all over the world because something wasn't right. Something definitely was not a "god" of mercy, and love, and justice, let alone ANYTHING good.

After a solid year of looking, reading, visiting various temples and churches and places of worship and speaking with the religious authorities at those places I'd made up my mind. It was bullshit. I can't tell you that there ISN'T an all mighty sky beard up there, just like you can't realistically disprove the flying spaghetti monster. I can however say that if their is one I don't much see a reason to worship it. Children with Leukemia? Brain tumors? Fucking Malaria? Seriously? All the evil and suffering in the world and you want me to believe that there's any being out there that is good and just and all powerful that allows that kind of shit when it would have the power to stop it? No, simply not the case. Either it is out there and is not all knowing, and not all powerful, so why should I worship it? OR if it is all powerful and all knowing, then it isn't a force for anything but evil, and why would I ever want to worship that.

Personally, I'll stick to my disbelief and being a good person and avoid the iron age and older mythologies.
